calls.reasoning: Guidance is +9-11% YoY on $102.466B (about $111.7-113.7B), with a 2.5pt FX headwind and tighter supply. Consensus is $112.95-113.6B. Apple has beaten its guide midpoint by about +1.6pp on average over the last 4 quarters, but this quarter is supply-constrained and iPhone 18 Pro had only about 9 days of sales in it. Median $113.7B, slightly above consensus. Missing the bottom of the guide (<$112B) is about 10%; >$118B needs a Q1-FY26-style blowout, about 3%. No human market on total revenue was found; Polymarket's thin product-line markets agree with consensus.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on every material fact: guidance +9-11% ($111.7-113.7B), 2.5pt FX headwind, supply constraints, consensus $112.95-113.6B, and Apple's record against guidance. The one factual gap is the Q2 FY26 guidance range, flagged as unverified in Run 2; it cannot be settled without web access and has little weight. What remains are judgment calls: the chance of landing below $112B (9-14%) and the median ($113.6-113.8B). Apple has fallen below its guide range only marginally recently (Q4 FY25 at 7.9% vs 8-10%), so I take 10% below-range; above-range needs about 15% growth, so 3%. I agree with the runs' reference class and dispersion width.
